We need to produce a test class for JsonSchema.getValidationContext(). The method simply returns the private field validationContext. We need to test that it returns the same instance passed in constructor.

We need to create JsonSchema instance. However constructors are private. There's a static factory method JsonSchema.from(...). But that is also package-private? It is static default (no modifier) – in same package com.networknt.schema, we can call it. In test class in same package, we can access package-private static method. So we can use JsonSchema.from(validationContext, schemaLocation, evaluationPath, schemaNode, parent, false). Need to create stub objects for parameters: ValidationContext, SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode (schemaNode), JsonSchema parent (maybe null). Need to create minimal objects.

We can mock ValidationContext using Mockito. But JsonSchema.from expects ValidationContext, SchemaLocation, JsonNodePath, JsonNode, JsonSchema, boolean. It also uses validationContext inside constructor for many operations like resolveSchemaId, getMetaSchema, etc. If we mock ValidationContext to return null for methods used to avoid NPE. In constructor, they call this.validationContext.resolveSchemaId(this.schemaNode); So we need to stub resolveSchemaId to return null. Also validationContext.getMetaSchema().readAnchor etc. So getMetaSchema must return a mock JsonMetaSchema with readAnchor returning null, readDynamicAnchor returning null. Also validationContext.getSchemaResources() returns a ConcurrentMap; we can provide a real map. So we can create a real ValidationContext with real JsonMetaSchema? That's more complex.

Simpler: Use Mockito to mock ValidationContext, and stub methods used in constructor to return safe values. But constructor also accesses validationContext.getSchemaResources() etc. So we need to stub getSchemaResources() to return a new ConcurrentHashMap<>. Similarly getDynamicAnchors() and getSchemaReferences(). Also getMetaSchema() returns mock JsonMetaSchema where readAnchor and readDynamicAnchor return null. Also getMetaSchema().readAnchor is called; also getMetaSchema().readDynamicAnchor. Also getMetaSchema().readAnchor returns null; fine.

Also validationContext.getJsonSchemaFactory() maybe used later but not in constructor. Not needed.

Also validationContext.getMetaSchema().readAnchor etc. So stub.

Also validationContext.getMetaSchema() used for getMetaSchema().readAnchor, readDynamicAnchor, also maybe other methods later but not in constructor.

Also validationContext.getMetaSchema().readAnchor may be called on null schemaNode? but fine.

Also validationContext.getMetaSchema() may be used later but not needed.

Thus we can create mocks.

Need SchemaLocation: we can create new SchemaLocation(null, null) but constructors require AbsoluteIri and JsonNodePath. We can pass null for both? The constructor expects AbsoluteIri absoluteIri, JsonNodePath fragment. Both can be null (no restrictions). So we can use new SchemaLocation(null, null). However there is also a constructor with only AbsoluteIri. We'll use new SchemaLocation(null, null).

JsonNodePath: new JsonNodePath(PathType.ROOT?) Actually constructor expects PathType type. PathType is an enum inside JsonNodePath? Not given. But we can use reflection? Might be internal. Simpler: mock JsonNodePath.

JsonNode schemaNode: mock JsonNode.

Parent JsonSchema: null.

Thus we can call JsonSchema.from(validationContext, schemaLocation, evaluationPath, schemaNode, null, false). This returns a JsonSchema instance.

Now test getValidationContext returns the same validationContext mock.

Write test method testGetValidationContextReturnsSameInstance.

Also maybe test that multiple calls return same instance.

So:
